A. Cl⁻: Chloride ion (Cl⁻) is formed when a chlorine atom gains one electron. Chlorine (Cl) has an atomic number of 17, so its neutral electronic configuration is 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁵. When it gains an electron to become Cl⁻, its configuration becomes 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶. This matches the given configuration.

B. K: Potassium (K) has an atomic number of 19, so its electronic configuration is 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁶4s¹. This does not match the given configuration.

C. Mg²⁺: Magnesium ion (Mg²⁺) is formed when a magnesium atom loses two electrons. Magnesium (Mg) has an atomic number of 12, so its neutral electronic configuration is 1s²2s²2p⁶3s². When it loses two electrons to become Mg²⁺, its configuration becomes 1s²2s²2p⁶. This does not match the given configuration.

D. Ne: Neon (Ne) has an atomic number of 10, so its electronic configuration is 1s²2s²2p⁶. This does not match the given configuration.

Therefore, the correct answer is A. Cl⁻.
